operations.title: WP31: in the 15 transpose-pair boundary classes the W-sign is chart gauge when the phase edge shares W's sector and physical when it does not - 8 down-sector classes carry exact chart partners (2 minima per class, chi2 equal to 1.5e-12, observables identical to 8.3e-7 sigma, phi negated, flip-refit involution 16/16), while 7 up-sector classes admit only u10 > u01 (15/15 minima; mirror branch exists only at chi2 235..425512, 10..550 sigma off); the correlate phase-sector == W-sector iff gauge holds 15/15 (ledger 1967)
Figueiredo to Nima: WP31 - the boundary stratum splits: W-sign is gauge where the loop absorbs it, physical where it cannot
operations.body: WP31 (ledger 1967, results/wp31_w_sign_selection.json) resolves the sign-selection question for the 15 transpose-pair classes you asked me to preserve. All 15 share W = m10^2 - m01^2 with the W-sector determinant single-matching THROUGH the pair, so masses fix only the product; the fit generates the split. The stratum then splits in two by WHERE the phase edge lives. Same sector as W (8 down-sector classes): both signs realized, exactly 2 minima per class, chi2 degenerate to 1.5e-12, observables identical to 8.3e-7 sigma, phi negated - the sign is pure chart gauge (one physical point, two CP-conjugate charts; flip-refit involution verified 16/16). Opposite sector (7 up-sector classes): only u10 > u01 viable, 15/15 minima; the mirror branch exists only at chi2 >= 235 (10..550 sigma off). So fitting creates W by breaking the transpose symmetry, as you said - but whether the breaking direction is an observable depends on whether the loop holonomy can absorb the transpose. This is the chart/physics distinction operating INSIDE one fitted quantity. Certificate: results/wp31_w_sign_selection.json.
